open.problem: THE PRICE IN THE CONFIRM DIALOG IS NOT THE PRICE CHARGED, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS SILENT. The client prices a haul itself and the server prices it again from a different median sample; only the server's number reaches wallet_charge. DRIVEN ON BOTH SIDES OF THE SEAM: on the live database I put one carrier with a delivered contract to a non-self shipper at base 400 and two never-delivered charters at base 20 (a normal market: shells undercut to win their first job). transport_quote(null,'N-A','N-B',2,10,false) then returns price 20000 — median 400 → Meridian base 1000. Handed the identical three rows that listCarriers() returns, routes.js answers medianTariff 20, tariffCap 100, meridianQuote price 2000. Driving the shipped module end-to-end through a DOM shim, the gcConfirm text is verbatim `Ship for 2,000 🔥? ETA 1h 20m.`, the RPC that then goes out is transport_dispatch({p_carrier_id:null, p_rig_id:null, p_from_node:'N-A', p_to_node:'N-B', p_hops:2, p_units:10, p_cargo:{metal:10}, p_escort:false, p_client_ref:…}) — the same arguments the server priced at 20000 — and the success toast is `🚛 Cargo dispatched.` with no figure at all. The player agreed to 2,000 and the wallet is debited 20,000; index.js never reads r.price, which holds the real number. It is wrong in both directions and only coincidentally right: at launch, with no delivered contract anywhere, the server's median is null and falls to meridian_base_floor 40 (Meridian 100/unit·hop) while any live board of player carriers above 40 makes the client quote MORE than is charged. routes.js's own drift ledger (D3) names this exactly — "the client can display a ceiling — and therefore a capped price — BELOW what transport_quote charges… shown one price, billed another in the bad direction" — and states the standing mitigation as "once a round trip has happened, prefer transport_quote's own returned price over this file's". That mitigation is not implemented: `grep -n "transport_quote" public/src/transport/*.js` returns only comments. The rate-board banner added in round 3 ("the exchange re-prices the haul when you dispatch it") discloses the risk in small print but does not stop the money dialog from stating a number nothing honours. Player-carrier quotes are hit by the same clamp whenever the price reaches either side's ceiling.
open.fix: Price the confirm off the server. transport_quote is already `grant execute … to authenticated` (sql/038:2214) and takes exactly the six values index.js holds at that moment (p_carrier_id, p_from_node, p_to_node, p_hops, p_units, p_escort) — call it in the 'quote'/'meridian' branch and put ITS price into S.quote, so the dialog and the charge come from one expression. If a second round trip is unwanted, the one-line floor is to stop the overcharge being silent: at index.js:1430 print what actually landed — `b.toast('🚛 Cargo dispatched — charged ' + fmtNum(num(r.price)) + ' 🔥.')` — and, when num(r.price) !== num(q.price), say so explicitly rather than letting the difference pass unmentioned. Do not try to reproduce the server's sample client-side; routes.js's header is right that the client cannot see which carriers have delivered.

open.problem: THE 15-SECOND REPAINT TICKER WIPES WHATEVER THE PLAYER IS TYPING. While the overlay is open, startTicker() calls paint() every 15,000 ms with only a `busy` guard, and paint() does `ov.innerHTML = html` — which destroys every <input> in the panel and the focus with them. depot.render.js:567 and :569 emit the two Depot-tab fields with no value at all: driving renderTransport() over the real view shape, the depot tab returns `mt-name value=""` and `mt-tariff value=""` on every call, because nothing on the pinned view carries them. So a player who takes longer than a tick to type a carrier name loses the name mid-word, the caret jumps to <body>, and the next keystrokes go nowhere. The five exchange fields are echoed (`mt-from value="N-A"`, `mt-cargo-n value="10"`, …) but only from S.form, which is written in exactly one place — the quote branch at index.js:1355 — so freshly typed route/units values that have not been quoted yet are lost by the same tick and silently replaced by the previous quote's values. depot.render.js's own comment at :921 records that paint() destroying these inputs was already a shipped defect once; the view.form echo closed the after-an-action case and left the timer case open.
open.fix: Skip the timed repaint while a field is being edited, using index.html's own test (index.html:36492): inside startTicker's callback, before paint(), `try { var ae = document.activeElement; if (ae && (ae.tagName === 'INPUT' || ae.tagName === 'TEXTAREA' || ae.isContentEditable)) return; } catch (e) {}`. Note this is the TICKER only — the post-action paint() in onClick's finally must keep repainting. It is worth adding mt-name/mt-tariff to the view echo in the same edit so a repaint from any source restores them, since those two are the entry point to the whole feature.

open.where: public/src/transport/contracts.js:1248 (`p_depot_level: null`) ↔ public/src/city/production.data.js:453-457 (the Freight Depot cost ladder) ↔ sql/038_transport_companies.sql transport_caps / transport_set_sheet
open.problem: UPGRADING THE FREIGHT DEPOT COSTS A FORTUNE AND BUYS NOTHING. Every cap the exchange enforces — reach in transport_quote, bays in transport_dispatch, fleet_cap in the transport_rigs BEFORE INSERT trigger — is read from transport_caps(), which computes them from transport_companies.depot_level, and NOTHING in the shipped client ever writes that column: setTariff() is the only caller of transport_set_sheet and passes `p_depot_level: null`, which the function coalesces back to the stored value (grep p_depot_level across /src/transport — one call site, one null). MEASURED ON THE LIVE DATABASE: for a real charter row, transport_caps returns {bays:2, reach:4, fleet_cap:4} and stays there; calling transport_set_sheet(co, null, null, 3, null) — which no code does — immediately returns {bays:6, reach:6, fleet_cap:12}. MEASURED ON THE CLIENT: with a level-3 freightdepot placed, depot.js reports bays 6, fleet 12, reach 6, and buildingCostAt() prices those upgrades at 83,333 🔥 + 538 metal / 400 supplies / 300 stone / 175 fuel / 200 wood for L2 and 195,000 🔥 + 1,150 metal / 850 supplies / 650 stone / 388 fuel / 438 wood / 23 memory shards for L3. The player pays that, takes on a real city load (draw scales with level: 54⚡, 24 crew, 12💧, 42☣ at L3, which browns out the rest of their city), and the exchange still refuses the fifth rig as `fleet_cap` and the fifth hop as `out_of_reach`. depotReady()'s drift arm states this honestly — but only inside the Freight Depot panel, AFTER the building has been bought; /src/city's blueprint card, where the money is actually spent, says nothing.
open.fix: Send the level. The server side already works and is bounded (`greatest(1, least(3, coalesce(p_depot_level, v_co.depot_level)))`), so this is a client-only change: publish depotReady().level through transport_set_sheet — either as a fourth argument on the existing setTariff() call or as a small publishDepotLevel() run on refresh when depotReady().drift includes 'level' — and delete the driftLevel arm in depot.js in the same edit, as its own comment instructs. If shipping the send is out of scope for this release, the disclosure has to move to where the Cinder leaves: make the Freight Depot's `desc` in production.data.js:330 say plainly that levels 2 and 3 raise the city's draw but do not yet raise anything the freight exchange enforces.

open.where: sql/038_transport_companies.sql:2753 and :2761 (transport_settle computes `v_bal` = sum over the carrier's whole ledger and returns it as `carrier_balance`), against sql/038_transport_companies.sql:1831-1838 (the tld_sel policy and the comment stating the rule)
open.problem:
THE RLS POLICY ON THE LEDGER IS BYPASSED BY THE RPC'S OWN RETURN VALUE. §3's tld_sel comment states the rule in as many words: "LEDGER · read. The company's owner, and nobody else — not even the shipper who paid for the line item. A shipper can already read the price on their own contract; what they must not get is the carrier's whole book, which is every price that carrier has ever accepted and therefore the floor of every future negotiation." The policy enforces exactly that (`using (public.is_transport_owner(company_id))`). transport_settle then computes `select coalesce(sum(amount), 0) into v_bal from public.transport_ledger where company_id = v_ct.carrier_id` — a SECURITY DEFINER read that bypasses tld_sel — and puts it in the success payload, which goes to WHOEVER SETTLED. §4.3's own header says "Either party may settle, because arrival is offline-safe", and the ownership test at :2637 passes the shipper as readily as the carrier. So the shipper gets, in one number, the aggregate the policy exists to hide.

DRIVEN on the live cluster as three separate `authenticated` roles against one carrier (Victim Haulage, owner user 1):
  · user 2 shipped a private 2000-unit haul, fare 40000, and settled it.
  · user 3 then shipped the CHEAPEST LEGAL haul — 5 units, 4 hops, price 100, the min_price_per_contract floor — and settled it.
  · user 3's own read of transport_ledger under RLS returns 0 rows (the policy works).
  · user 3's transport_settle payload returns `"carrier_balance": 58100`.
That 58100 contains user 2's 40000 and an earlier third-party 18000 — two other shippers' private fares — for 100 Cinder. Repeating it is a running meter: the delta between two readings is exactly what that carrier earned from everyone else in between, which is the negotiation floor the comment names.

WHAT GATES IT TODAY, stated so this is not read as bigger than it is: the shipper must be someone other than the carrier's owner, which needs a cross-player contract, which needs a rig uuid in that carrier's fleet — and transport_dispatch refuses a null p_rig_id (:2372) and claims the run under `r.company_id = p_carrier_id` (:2403) while trg_sel (:1670) keeps rig rows owner-only, so a stranger cannot get one. index.js:1191 ownRigRowId() returns '' for any carrier but your own and index.js:1410 refuses the dispatch client-side with a sentence. So the reachable case today is self-haul, where the settler already owns the book. It opens for every customer the moment dispatch chooses the rig itself or a free-rigs view is published — the two options index.js:1164-1170 names as the real fix — and it will open silently, because nothing in §4.3 mentions the ledger policy.
open.fix: Gate the key the same way §2 gated transport_caps' fleet_used and §4.2 gated the run counter — keys ABSENT for a non-owner, not null: `'carrier_balance', case when v_ct.carrier_id is not null and public.is_transport_owner(v_ct.carrier_id) then v_bal end` (or build the base object and `|| case when … then jsonb_build_object('carrier_balance', v_bal) else '{}'::jsonb end`, which is the shape transport_caps already uses at :1284-1293). Nothing regresses on the client: `carrier_balance` is read exactly once anywhere under public/ — contracts.js:1690 copies it into a `carrierBalance` field of settleContract()'s return — and grep for `carrierBalance` across public/ finds no consumer of that field at all, so the value is already dead on the wire. Skip the `select … into v_bal` entirely when the caller is not the owner while you are there. Cite :1831-1838 in the comment so the next reader sees the return value and the policy were written to one rule, and add the ledger to the §4.3 header's list of what settle may hand back.

open.where: sql/038_transport_companies.sql:2482 (the stranger's bare `rig_out_of_runs`) read against the ordering of :2399-2409 (the run claim) and :2503 (the charge), and against the header's claim at :523-528
open.problem:
THE ROUND-3 FIX GATED THE NUMBERS BUT NOT THE FACT, AND THE PROBE IS NOW FREE RATHER THAN COSTING A HAUL. The security header now claims this channel closed: "transport_dispatch's refusal path splits owner from stranger the same way the §2b guard does… Closes: the THIRD read channel on a rival's yard — a SECURITY DEFINER re-read that bypasses trg_sel and answers a stranger's poll of a rig's daily counter, for the price of one haul, and only when the rig is spent" (:523-528). Two halves of that are not true of the delivered code. (a) The bare code `rig_out_of_runs` IS the protected fact. trg_sel's rule is not "how many runs are left" but "knowing a carrier is out of runs is knowing exactly when to undercut them" (:1666-1668) — a boolean, and it is precisely what the bare code returns. (b) It no longer costs a haul: the run claim (:2399) runs BEFORE wallet_charge (:2503), so a caller who cannot afford the fare still reaches the claim and is discriminated by which refusal comes back.

DRIVEN, as `authenticated` user 2 with a wallet balance of 0, against user 1's carrier and rig:
  · rig with runs left  → `{"ok": false, "error": "insufficient_cinder", "needed": 100, "balance": 0}`
  · same rig once spent → `{"ok": false, "error": "rig_out_of_runs"}`, twice in a row
After both polls: attacker balance still 0, `transport_contracts` count 0, and the victim's rig unchanged at runs_used 1 / status idle — the unwind at :2551 puts the claimed run straight back. So it is an unlimited, perfectly reliable, zero-cost binary oracle on the exact fact, not a paid one, and the wallet does not even need to be empty — any balance below the fare gives the same discrimination.

SAME GATE AS THE FINDING ABOVE, and it is why this is minor rather than moderate: the poll needs a rig uuid in that carrier's fleet, and trg_sel (:1670) plus the `r.company_id = p_carrier_id` claim (:2403) mean a stranger cannot get one today. It becomes free and aimable the moment a shipper legitimately holds a rival's rig_id — which tct_sel (:1818) grants on the shipper's own contract row the first time a cross-player haul is possible.
open.fix: Two cheap options, and the file should pick one rather than leave the header's claim standing. Narrow: move the affordability probe ahead of the run claim — call `public.wallet_charge` only after the claim as now, but check the shipper's balance against v_price before claiming, so the two refusals cannot be told apart by a caller who never intended to pay. Blunt and simpler: fold the non-owner arm's `rig_out_of_runs` into the same code the other unaimable membership probes already return, so a stranger cannot distinguish "spent" from "not in this fleet" at all — the client degrades correctly either way, since contracts.js's explain() renders a code with no detail keys. Whichever is chosen, correct :523-528: it currently asserts a channel is closed that is narrowed, and asserts a price ("for the price of one haul") the delivered ordering does not charge. A security-relevant claim that overstates what the code does is the failure mode this file's own header spends its length arguing against, and it is the sentence that will stop the next reader looking.

open.problem: "REPAIRABLE MIRRORS transport_repair()'s OWN REFUSALS, ONE FOR ONE, so the button is never offered for a call that cannot succeed. The RPC … refuses THREE things, and this expression is those three and nothing else." transport_repair refuses NINE: not_authenticated, closed (:2813), no_such_rig, not_your_rig (:2821), rig_in_transit, rig_retired (:2831), rig_is_salvage (:2834), not_damaged (:2839) and repair_cap (:2860). At least `not_damaged` is decidable from data already on the view row. c_ladder is array['Wrecked','Battered','Worn','Clean','Pristine'] (:2805) and :2837-2841 refuses `not_damaged` when `v_i >= array_length(c_ladder,1)` — i.e. for condition 'Pristine'. `grep -n Pristine public/src/transport/depot.render.js` returns nothing, and the guard at :846 is `!!vid && !salvaged && status !== 'retired' && status !== 'hauling'`, so Repair renders ENABLED on a Pristine rig. index.js's onClick 'repair' arm (:1450-1469) tests only the id crossing, and contracts.js repair() SPENDS FIRST — gcConfirm, then takeRes(bill.parts) at :1745 and spendGems(bill.cinder) at :1751 — before the RPC. So the exact spend/refuse/unwind round trip this comment says the mirror exists to prevent is live, and reachable on the ordinary path: the free starter rig is minted at 'Clean' (index.html:80557), one repair takes it to 'Pristine', the next click charges, refunds, and toasts CODES.not_damaged ("That rig is already Pristine. Nothing to repair."). `repair_cap` is the same class one step out — listMyRigs selects repairs_used but not repair_day (contracts.js:1084), so the panel cannot mirror that one even if it wanted to.
open.fix: Add the missing state test to the guard at depot.render.js:846 — a positive "has a rung above it" test against c_ladder rather than a `!== 'Pristine'` literal, so a future sixth rung does not silently re-open it. Then rewrite the comment at :800-812 to say what it now is: transport_repair refuses nine things, this expression mirrors the FOUR that are decidable from a fleet row (rig_in_transit, rig_retired, rig_is_salvage, not_damaged), and repair_cap is knowingly not mirrored because repair_day is not in listMyRigs's select list. Record the not_damaged miss the way the block already records bugs (1)-(3), rather than correcting the count silently. The duplicate "deny list of three refusals" claim at :1315-1317 has to move with it.

open.problem: index.js quotes, in the present tense and as the server's current guarantee, a sentence sql/038 retracted in this very round as a false safety property: "Direction of failure chosen deliberately, and it matches sql/038 ~598: 'if the two ever disagree the carrier gets FEWER runs than the UI promised.'" sql/038:835-846 is that column's comment and it now reads "⚠ THIS COMMENT USED TO SAY THE SERVER 'honours least(runs_cap, transport_config.max_runs_per_rig), so if the two ever disagree the carrier gets FEWER runs than the UI promised…' THE DIRECTION IS RIGHT AND THE CLAMP NEVER BINDS" — max_runs_per_rig defaults to 10 (:1106) and the column CHECK is `between 1 and 10` (:875), so least() cannot reduce anything a client can write.
